subject: Hosted inference SLO: measurement approach & edge-case rationale
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@finly.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted inference SLO: measurement approach & edge-case rationale

Alex — thanks again for the sync this morning. Per our conversation I'm attaching a concise proposal for how Redwood would define and measure P50/P95 latency commitments for the hosted inference product. High level summary below and the attached PDF has the full definition and sample metric queries.

Quick summary (proposal):
- Commitment: P50 = 60ms, P95 = 250ms for text-generation API (resp. tokens) for the "standard" model profile.
- Measurement windows: compute rolling 1-hour percentiles per route, then report a daily aggregated P50/P95 computed from those 1-hour buckets (24 values per day).
- Carve-outs: exclude cold-starts where instance lifetime < 60s, exclude requests served entirely from prefix/KV cache (cache-hit flag), transient region failovers (documented in outage log).
- Route segmentation: per-customer route-level SLOs optional — default SLO applies to "/v1/generate" and "/v1/chat" flows; heavy-batch/streaming endpoints are tracked but scoped separately.

Why the 1-hour rolling buckets? Two reasons: 1) preserves an SLO that's robust to brief, high-amplitude spikes (e.g., multi-minute bursty traffic) while still surfacing systemic regressions; 2) keeps the reported daily P95 from flipping wildly during short incident windows while maintaining sensitivity to repeated degradations.

Open items for Finly to confirm:
1) Acceptable carve-out threshold for warm-starts (we proposed 60s).
2) Whether Finly prefers a 7-day rolling window for contractual violations (we currently report daily but can aggregate 7-day violation rate).
3) Any route-level minimum throughput requirement to be eligible for measurement (we currently require >= 100 requests/hour).

I've attached the SLO proposal (slo-proposal-v1.pdf) with the exact metric names and sample PromQL-style queries. If this looks good I can ask Rishi to produce a sample 7-day violations table scoped to your production traffic next week.

Thanks — Ben

Subject: Re: Hosted inference SLO: measurement approach & edge-case rationale

Ben — thanks for the write-up and the PDF. A few quick reactions from our side:

- P50/P95 numbers look reasonable, but our legal team will push for tighter P50 for product-facing routes (they asked for P50=40ms). Can we show the distribution for first-party vs third-party traffic?
- Concern about the 1-hour bucket: we've seen short bursts that last ~7-10 minutes that materially impact user experience; if you average at 1 hour the spike gets smoothed and isn't visible in the daily rollup. Would you be able to provide a paired metric: 10-minute rolling buckets (for alerting/visibility) + 1-hour buckets for contractual measurement?
- Also want clarity on retries: are retries from clients counted as separate requests? We need to ensure retry storms don't penalize Redwood for things on our side.

Two asks: can you add a short paragraph that explicitly describes how retries and client-side backoff are treated? And can you provide a sample 7-day rolling violation example so our procurement team can see how the contract clause behaves over time?

If it's helpful let's do a 30-minute call tomorrow to align before I pass to legal.

— Alex
Alex Reynolds
Head of Platform, Finly
alex.reynolds@finly.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-18T13:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted inference SLO: measurement approach & edge-case rationale

Appreciate the quick feedback, Alex — good points. Answers inline and next steps below.

- P50 split for product-facing routes: We can surface per-route P50; default contract will reference the overall "standard" route but we can append an appendix that shows route-specific baselines for Finly's first-party traffic. I'll ask Rishi for a route-level report.

- 10-minute buckets: Absolutely — that aligns with your concern. Proposal change: we keep contractual computation on 1-hour buckets (to limit churn in daily reports) AND produce a complementary 10-minute rolling percentile series for alerting and for your visibility. Contract language will state that the 10-minute series is for operational diagnostics and not for counting a contractual violation. Example phrasing: "Contractual SLO violations are measured on 1-hour aggregation buckets; operational alerting may use 10-minute rolling percentiles and is not a basis for settlement."

- Retries: We propose counting each ingress request as an individual API call for observability, but for contractual violation calculations we will deduplicate client-initiated retries if they contain the same client-request-id header within a 30s window. If Finly cannot supply client-request-id consistently, we will default to dedup via source IP + identical request fingerprint within 15s and document that in Appendix B.

Next steps: Rishi will generate a 7-day mock violation report against a sampled window of your traffic, and Marissa will prepare a redline for the SLO clause with the updated 10-minute/1-hour language. Can we schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow at 10:00am PT?

Thanks — Ben

Alex — looped in as promised. Ben laid out a pragmatic approach here; I've redlined the SLO clause and attached the document (slo-clause-redline.docx) with two small edits:

1) Explicitly call out the client-request-id dedupe mechanism and the fallback fingerprint rule, with an example.
2) Add an operational carve-out for scheduled maintenance windows (we propose standard 2h/week maintenance windows that are pre-notified and excluded from violation calculations).

Also, for procurement comfort we've added a 14-day remediation SLA for any verified systemic regressions that cause an elevated violation rate (this is a commercial concession Finly may want to negotiate). If you prefer, we can present the contract language as either a hard SLA or a commercial credit table — whichever procurement prefers.

I'm available for the 10:00am PT call tomorrow; Ben/Rishi please send the calendar invite.

Thanks — Marissa
